thread:
omar: Quick dump from the heatmap probe — small-batch behavior across regions for reranker/embeds. link: https://internal.redwood/bench/2067890123 (pdf + raw csv)
sophia: Saw the link. Which GPUs and dims were in this run?
omar: Ran A100-40GB (us-east), H100 (eu-west), and a c7g-like CPU spot (apac) for comparison. Dims: 128 / 256 / 512 / 1024. Batch sizes focused on 1,2,4,8 (smallbatch). Quant: fp16, int8 (post-quant), and 4-bit (Q4) for a subset.
lena: TL;DR: for embed dim=256, batch=4:
- A100 us p95 ~ 6.2ms, throughput ~ 14k qps (vectorized path)
- H100 eu p95 ~ 5.8ms, throughput ~ 16k qps
- CPU apac p95 ~ 48ms, throughput ~ 1.2k qps
p99 spikes on H100 in apac region due to kernel fallback on long seqs.
kai: Noted a weird kernel mismatch on eu-west H100: flash-attn enabled in compile but fallback to generic kernel for certain dim/batch combos -> p99 jump. We saw this when dims==1024 and batch==1, likely memory-alignment edge-case.
build-bot: bench-runner: finished run 2067890123, artifacts at s3://bench-artifacts/2067890123/, logs at /ci/bench/2067890123.log
sophia: Do you have the heatmap for p95 vs batch/dim? The PDF link had a noisy legend.
omar: Pasted the key slice of the heatmap (p95 latency ms) for embeds: `dims x batch`
```
       b1   b2   b4   b8
128   2.1  2.6  3.8  6.9
256   3.4  4.8  7.1 12.6
512   5.9  8.7 13.2 25.1
1024 11.8 18.9 31.0 58.7
```
This is for A100 us. H100 numbers scale ~0.9x for small batches except p99 spikes in EU for 1024.
lena: On quant: int8 gives ~1.15x throughput bump on GPU for embed dims <=512, but Q4 is hit-or-miss; some kernels don't have Q4 fast paths -> fallback slower than fp16 for large dims.
sre-bot: For capacity planning, what's the recommended headroom for Dedicated pool (per-region) if customer expects 10k qps of dim=256 embeddings with batch=4?
omar: Quick calc: using A100 numbers ~14k qps per node (advertised run), but that's with ideal packing and persistent KV cache. Real-world safe capacity per node = 0.6 * peak -> ~8.4k qps. So for 10k qps you need 2 nodes per region (or 1 + autoscale buffer). Add 30% for cold starts & variance -> recommend 3 nodes for strict SLA.
sophia: Can we automate a small int8 microbench for dims {256,512} and batch {1,2,4} across regions and post results to the metrics dashboard? I can wire a nightly job.
kai: Yes, but add a check for kernel fallback: if we see >1 fallback per 1k requests, flag the build and add the problematic kernel config to the ticket.
lena: Here's the bench command I used locally (copyable):
```
python tools/run_bench.py \
  --model rerank-open-003 \
  --mode embed \
  --dims 256,512 \
  --batches 1,2,4 \
  --quant int8,fp16 \
  --iterations 2000 \
  --report s3://bench-artifacts/2067890123/
```
Sample output snippet:
```
[embed] dim=256 batch=4 quant=int8 mean=0.071ms per-token p95=4.8ms throughput=14300 qps
[embed] dim=512 batch=1 quant=fp16 mean=0.12ms per-token p95=5.9ms throughput=9200 qps
```
sophia: Nice. For the dashboard, let's surface p50/p95/p99 + fallback-rate + kernel-id. That'll make regressions obvious.
omar: Agreed. Next steps: (1) schedule nightly microbench for int8 small-batch in eu/us/apac, (2) add kernel-fallback alarm, (3) run a canary with dedicated pool at ~50% expected load to validate capacity calc.
lena: I can own (1) and (3). Will open a PR for the job and a canary playbook.
kai: I will add kernel-id tagging to the runtime logs so bench results correlate with kernel path.
sophia: Great, thanks team. If anyone wants the raw csv I can dump it to a temp bucket and share.
omar: sharing now: s3://bench-artifacts/temp/2067890123/raw.csv :thumbsup:
